q: How do you compute several metrics (counts, conditional sums, rates) in one query?
a: Conditional aggregation: SUM(CASE WHEN cond THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) for counts, SUM(CASE WHEN cond THEN amount ELSE 0 END) for conditional sums, AVG(CASE WHEN cond THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) for rates, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN cond THEN user_id END) for unique users.

q: What's wrong with COUNT(CASE WHEN cond THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)?
a: COUNT counts every non-NULL value, and 0 isn't NULL, so it counts all rows. Use SUM instead, or drop the ELSE so non-matches become NULL.

q: How do you pivot rows into columns in SQL?
a: Group by the row key and use one conditional aggregate per output column, e.g. SUM(CASE WHEN status='completed' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS completed. Works in every dialect (some have a PIVOT keyword too).

q: How do you compute each group's percentage of the total?
a: 100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () — the window sums the group counts across all groups. Or divide by a scalar subquery of the total.

q: Find customers who bought every product in a category.
a: Relational division: GROUP BY customer, HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE category = …).
